intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the sensory overload of Marrakech's iconic main square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then witness the square transform into a massive open-air food market at sunset. Wander the labyrinthine souks of the ancient medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handcrafted lanterns.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber desert camp. Spend the night under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake at dawn to watch the sun rise over the dunes in total silence.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided or local-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellij tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then visit the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class in a Riad
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class hosted inside a traditional riad courtyard. Visit the local spice market with your host, then learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes including tagine, harira soup, and bastilla. Enjoy your creations over a communal lunch and take home handwritten recipes.

experiences.name: Atlas Mountains Day Hike via Imlil Village
experiences.description: Take a short transfer from Marrakech to the Berber village of Imlil at the foot of Mount Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak. Hike through walnut groves, terraced fields, and traditional mountain villages. Meet local Berber families, enjoy a home-cooked lunch, and take in sweeping panoramic views of the High Atlas range.
experiences.location: Imlil village, High Atlas Mountains, outside Marrakech

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the No. 19 public bus (approx. 4 MAD) or shared petit taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk around your neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Easy introduction to the Medina - stroll through the edges of Djemaa el-Fna square as the evening market comes alive. Watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers for free. Browse the night market stalls.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with honey or amlou from a street vendor near the Medina for 5-10 MAD
meals.dinner: Eat at the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls - try harira soup (5 MAD), kefta brochettes (15 MAD), and fresh orange juice (4 MAD). Budget around 40-60 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros or dollars to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina for better rates. Avoid official-looking touts outside the airport - use metered taxis or the public bus. Keep your bags close in the busy square.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (free to view from outside, non-Muslims cannot enter) and the surrounding gardens. Then head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning examples of Moroccan Islamic architecture - entrance fee approx. 70 MAD. Arrive early (opens at 9:00) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the souks of the Medina on foot - free to wander. Navigate the labyrinthine lanes of the spice souk, leather souk, and lantern souk. Practice your bargaining skills. Visit the Medersa Ali Ben Youssef area and the nearby Musée de Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD). Stop at the famous tanneries viewpoint for free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for sunset - the square transforms into a carnival of activity. Watch the Gnawa musicians perform (tip 5-10 MAD). Explore the surrounding streets of the northern Medina.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the hotel - mint tea, msemen, olive oil, and amlou for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap and filling lunch at a local hole-in-the-wall restaurant in the souks - try a tagine or couscous for 30-50 MAD
meals.dinner: Affordable sit-down dinner at a local restaurant off Djemaa el-Fna - pastilla or lamb tagine with bread for 60-80 MAD. Avoid tourist-facing restaurants on the main square which charge double.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes - the Medina streets are uneven and you will walk 8-12 km easily. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) as a sign of respect. A hand-drawn map or offline Google Maps is essential as the souks have no clear signage.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) - a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis. Then walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) for sweeping views and fascinating history of the once-magnificent 16th-century palace. Explore the storks nesting on the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD - worth it for the cobalt-blue architecture and exotic plants) or opt for the free Menara Gardens and its olive groves and pavilion reflecting pool if budget is tight. Walk along the ancient Medina walls (ramparts) for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Palmeraie (palm grove) on the outskirts of Marrakech - accessible by local bus or shared taxi. Return to the Medina for a relaxed evening of mint tea and people-watching at a rooftop café.

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices near the Rahba Kedima spice square - mint tea and Moroccan pancakes for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack lunch from street vendors near El Badi Palace - fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD), a sandwich with kefta (15 MAD), and a piece of chebakia pastry (5 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local neighbourhood restaurant outside the main tourist zone - chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, bread, and tea for 55-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden is owned by the Yves Saint Laurent estate and also houses a small Berber museum (included in ticket). If budget is very tight, the Menara Gardens offer similar tranquility for free. Tuesday mornings are less crowded at most sites.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - 2027-03-18 (Travel Day: Marrakech to Sahara Desert)
day_by_day.morning: Early departure at 06:00-07:00 from Marrakech. Book a shared group tour/shuttle to Merzouga (Sahara) in advance - budget options via shared minibus cost 150-250 MAD one way. The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas. Stop at a roadside Berber village for photos and tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') - brief stop to view the Kasbah Taourirt from the outside (free exterior view). Pass through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) and Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs and date palm oases. Arrive in Merzouga area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget desert camp on the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes. Ride a camel at sunset into the dunes (usually included in camp package or ~100-150 MAD separately). Watch the spectacular Saharan sunset over the orange dunes. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel before departure - bread, jam, and coffee for 15-20 MAD or pack snacks from a local shop
meals.lunch: Roadside stop lunch in a small town along the route - harira soup and bread for 20-30 MAD, or bring packed snacks to save money
meals.dinner: Included in most budget desert camp packages - traditional Berber tagine, bread, mint tea, and dried fruits around the campfire. If not included, budget 80-100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared transport and desert camp at least 2-3 days in advance from Marrakech. Budget desert camps in Merzouga cost 150-300 MAD per person per night including dinner and breakfast. The drive is approximately 9-10 hours total with stops - bring snacks, water, and a light jacket for the mountain pass. Shared group tours from Marrakech are the most budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 06:00) for the magical Sahara dawn - walk or ride a camel to a high dune to watch the sunrise over the Erg Chebbi dunes. This is one of the most breathtaking free experiences in Morocco. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Then explore the dunes on foot - try sandboarding (boards sometimes available at camp or rent for ~30-50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby village of Merzouga on foot or by local transport. Explore the village, interact with locals, and visit a fossil and mineral shop (no obligation to buy - the geology of the region is fascinating). Optional: visit a local Gnawa musician family for an authentic cultural experience (small tip appreciated, ~20-30 MAD). Rest at the camp during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Second sunset in the desert - climb the highest dune accessible from your camp for panoramic views of the endless sea of sand. Another evening of traditional music, storytelling, and stargazing around the campfire. The Sahara sky at night is extraordinary with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Included in camp package - Berber bread (khobz), olive oil, honey, argan jam, Moroccan tea
meals.lunch: Simple lunch at the camp or in Merzouga village - tagine or omelette sandwich for 30-50 MAD
meals.dinner: Included in camp package - communal Berber dinner around the fire with tagine, couscous, and mint tea

day_by_day.notes: March weather in the Sahara is ideal - warm days (20-25°C) and cool nights (5-10°C). Bring a warm layer for evenings and early mornings. Protect your electronics and eyes from sand. Bring enough cash as there are no ATMs in the desert camp area - the nearest ATM is in Erfoud or Rissani (15-20 km away). Stay hydrated and use sunscreen.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 - 2027-03-20 (Desert to Marrakech Return / Aït Benhaddou)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from the desert camp (around 07:00). Travel back westward with a significant stop at Aït Benhaddou - a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most spectacular fortified villages (ksour) in Morocco. Entrance to the ksar is free to walk through. Explore the ancient earthen towers, film location of Game of Thrones and Gladiator, and enjoy the view from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Ouarzazate for lunch and a brief stop. Optionally visit the Atlas Film Studios (entrance ~50 MAD) - one of the largest film studios in the world, used for many Hollywood productions. Then continue the drive back through the High Atlas Mountains toward Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (around 18:00-19:00). Check back into your accommodation, freshen up, and enjoy a final evening walk through the Medina. Visit a traditional hammam (public bathhouse) for a budget scrub and relaxation - public hammams cost only 15-25 MAD (bring your own soap and towel).

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp package before departure
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Ouarzazate - chicken tagine or kefta with bread for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech - treat yourself to a slightly nicer local restaurant for your second-to-last night. Try pastilla (sweet pigeon or chicken pie) for 60-90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is a must-see - try to arrive in the morning before tour buses crowd the site. Crossing the river to the ksar can be done via a small footbridge or by wading (in spring the water may be low). The return journey is approximately 9-10 hours with stops. Confirm your return transport the night before in the desert camp.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - 2027-03-21 (Final Day in Marrakech & Departure Prep)
day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech - visit any sites you missed earlier in the week. Recommended: the Mellah (old Jewish quarter) with its distinctive architecture and covered market, or the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) with its stunning 19th-century Andalusian-style courtyards and painted ceilings. Wander the quieter southern Medina streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks - best budget buys include argan oil, saffron, dried rose petals, leather goods, and hand-painted ceramics. Remember to bargain firmly (start at 30-40% of the asking price). Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Take a final mint tea on a rooftop café overlooking the Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time - take the No. 19 bus (4 MAD) or a shared taxi. Enjoy a final Moroccan meal before your flight if time permits. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and authentic Moroccan experiences.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café one last time - mint tea, msemen, honey, amlou, and hard-boiled eggs for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local Medina restaurant - bowl of harira, a briouate pastry, and fresh juice for 30-45 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport or pre-departure meal - grab a sandwich or snack for 20-30 MAD, or eat a proper last dinner near the hotel before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The No. 19 bus from Djemaa el-Fna to the airport takes about 30-45 minutes and is the most budget-friendly option. Keep some MAD for the bus but exchange remaining currency before leaving as Moroccan Dirhams cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: Day 1: ~100 MAD, Days 2-3: ~300-400 MAD/day, Day 4-5: ~400-500 MAD (including transport and camp), Day 6: ~300 MAD, Day 7: ~200-300 MAD.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk into the nearby medina edges. Visit Jemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere — street performers, orange juice vendors, and storytellers. Explore the surrounding souks gently without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a rooftop dinner overlooking Jemaa el-Fna. Watch the square transform into a vibrant night market with food stalls, musicians, and acrobats.

meals.breakfast: Skipped due to midday arrival — grab a light snack at the airport or upon arrival
meals.lunch: Café de France or a nearby café on Jemaa el-Fna square for a simple Moroccan sandwich or harira soup (~50–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant in the medina — mid-range Moroccan cuisine in a beautiful garden courtyard (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00. Allow 1–1.5 hours for immigration, baggage, and transfer to the hotel. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for rest and acclimatization. Exchange some currency at the airport or hotel for local spending.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the magnificent Bahia Palace (Palais Bahia) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and painted ceilings. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the nearby El Badi Palace ruins for sweeping views and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Saadian Tombs, a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis. Then stroll through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the historic Lazama Synagogue. End the afternoon at the vibrant spice market and dyers' souk in the medina.
day_by_day.evening: Take a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam (e.g., Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a medina bathhouse). Relax and unwind with a scrub and steam session (~150–250 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café — msemen (Moroccan pancakes), mint tea, and amlou (almond-argan spread)
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant near the Saadian Tombs — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop terrace views (~120–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a medina riad restaurant — try a traditional lamb tagine or couscous (~130–180 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: March weather in Marrakech is pleasant — expect temperatures around 18–24°C. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the medina's cobblestone streets. Book the hammam in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Majorelle Garden (Jardin Majorelle) — a cobalt-blue botanical oasis designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Also visit the adjacent Berber Museum (Museum of Moroccan Arts) within the garden complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Yves Saint Laurent Museum (MIAM) next to Majorelle for a fascinating intersection of fashion and Moroccan culture. Afterward, head to the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) for a different perspective — browse art galleries and modern Moroccan design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan music and folklore dinner show — gnawa music, belly dancing, and Berber performances in a dinner-theater setting.

meals.breakfast: Café Clock Marrakech — famous for their camel burger brunch and Moroccan breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the Mellah market — fresh bread, olives, cheeses, and seasonal fruits (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Chez Ali dinner show outside Marrakech — a classic tourist experience with folkloric entertainment and a traditional Moroccan feast (~250–350 MAD per person including show)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden entry is ~70 MAD; the Berber Museum is an additional ~30 MAD. Book the evening dinner show in advance as it's popular. This is a good day for photography enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 7:00 AM) by private or shared transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the scenic Dades Valley route. Drive through the High Atlas Mountains, passing through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) with breathtaking panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate — the 'Gateway to the Sahara' and Morocco's film capital. Stop at Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel and learn about its history from a local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes area) or Zagora depending on the route taken. Check into a mid-range desert camp or auberge. Enjoy a sunset camel ride into the dunes as the sky turns shades of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant stop in Ouarzazate — simple Moroccan menu with tagine and salad (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp under the stars — harira, tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (~150–200 MAD or included with camp)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — approximately 8–10 hours of driving with stops. Consider hiring a private driver for comfort and flexibility (~600–900 MAD for a shared transfer or ~1,200–1,800 MAD for private). Bring layers as desert temperatures drop significantly at night in March (can reach 5–8°C).

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes for a spectacular desert dawn — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Watch the sun rise over an endless sea of golden sand. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local Berber village of Merzouga on foot or by quad bike. Visit a local nomad family for authentic tea and conversation. Optionally take a sandboarding session on the dunes (equipment rental ~100–150 MAD). Visit a fossil and mineral shop — the Sahara region is famous for its ancient fossils.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a second night at the desert camp. Enjoy a bonfire, traditional drum circles (gnawa music), and stargazing in one of the world's best dark-sky locations far from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp — khobz bread, argan oil, honey, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local auberge in Merzouga village — Moroccan salads, tagine, and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Communal dinner at the desert camp around the bonfire — traditional Moroccan feast with live Berber music

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for daytime desert activities. March is an ideal month for the Sahara — not too hot (daytime ~22–28°C) and not too cold. Protect your camera from sand. This is the adventure highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert after breakfast and begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the Draa Valley — a different and equally scenic route lined with ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and traditional Berber villages. Stop at the Draa Valley's lush palm groves near Zagora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tinghir Oasis and the breathtaking Todgha Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls carved by the Todgha River. Take a short hike through the gorge and interact with local Berber guides. The gorge is also popular with rock climbers.
day_by_day.evening: Continue toward the Dades Gorge area or Boumalne Dades for an overnight stay at a mid-range guesthouse. Enjoy a quiet evening in this dramatic valley landscape.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Tinghir near the gorge — fresh trout from the river (a regional specialty), Moroccan salads (~100–140 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the guesthouse in Dades Valley — home-cooked Moroccan meal with regional specialties (~120–160 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is another long driving day (~6–7 hours with stops). The Todgha Gorge is most dramatic in the early afternoon light. Pack a light jacket for the gorge walk as it can be cool in the shade. The Dades Valley road (Route of a Thousand Kasbahs) offers incredible photo opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Final drive back to Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at a traditional Berber cooperative along the way to purchase authentic argan oil, rose water products, and handmade crafts directly from artisan producers at fair prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Marrakech by early afternoon. Spend final hours in the medina doing last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — leather goods, Moroccan lanterns, textiles, ceramics, and spices. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (if not visited earlier) — a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with exquisite zellij tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Marrakech at a special mid-range riad restaurant. Reflect on the journey over a leisurely Moroccan meal. If the flight is the next day, pack and prepare for departure; if departing late, head to Jemaa el-Fna one last time for a farewell evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Dades guesthouse before departure — Moroccan pancakes, honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Quick lunch stop en route — roadside café or packed lunch from the guesthouse (~60–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dar Zitoun or a similar riad restaurant in Marrakech medina — full traditional Moroccan spread with pastilla, tagine, and bastilla au lait dessert (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow enough time to return to Marrakech before any evening obligations. Bargaining in the souks is expected — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep some MAD for tips, last purchases, and airport expenses. The trip covers approximately 1,200–1,500 km total — an epic Moroccan adventure spanning imperial cities, mountain passes, ancient kasbahs, and the Sahara Desert.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in a chauffeured vehicle with welcome refreshments en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your suite. Enjoy a leisurely orientation tour of the property, followed by a relaxing afternoon at the resort's pool or hammam spa to recover from travel. Optional: a short stroll through the nearby Palmeraie gardens to acclimate to the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Private welcome dinner at the resort's signature rooftop restaurant, featuring panoramic views of the Atlas Mountains at dusk. Experience a curated tasting menu of modern Moroccan cuisine with a sommelier-selected wine and cocktail pairing.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or at airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze and mint tea served poolside upon arrival at the resort
meals.dinner: Rooftop tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant — expect dishes such as bastilla au pigeon, slow-braised lamb with preserved lemon, and orange blossom panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport and travel documents are ready for check-in. Request a late checkout confirmation for Day 7 if needed. Concierge will brief you on the full week's itinerary over welcome tea.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Medina of Marrakech — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Begin at the iconic Koutoubia Mosque (exterior), then wind through the labyrinthine souks with an expert local guide who will narrate the history of each quarter. Visit the spice markets, leather tanneries, and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive visit to the Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs with a private historian guide providing in-depth context on Moroccan dynastic history. Follow with a bespoke shopping experience in the upscale boutiques of Mouassine, where your concierge has pre-arranged private showroom access for Moroccan crafts, jewelry, and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a renowned riad restaurant in the Medina — a private courtyard setting with live Gnawa music performance. Experience traditional Moroccan hospitality with a multi-course diffa feast.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast at the resort: msemen flatbreads, amlou almond dip, fresh-pressed juices, pastilla pastries, and Berber omelette
meals.lunch: Private lunch at a heritage riad in the Medina — harira soup, kefta brochettes, and freshly baked khobz bread
meals.dinner: Diffa feast at a top-rated riad restaurant — pastilla, tagine of lamb with prunes and almonds, couscous royale, and a selection of Moroccan pastries with mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina exploration. The souks can be intense — your private guide ensures a relaxed, pressure-free experience. Dress modestly out of respect for local customs.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée YSL Marrakech). Explore the cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece with a private art and history guide. The museum offers extraordinary insight into the intersection of Moroccan culture and global fashion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Menara Gardens and its historic 12th-century pavilion overlooking the olive groves and Atlas Mountain backdrop — ideal for photography. Return to the resort for a traditional hammam and argan oil massage treatment at the spa (90-minute luxury package).
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private cooking class with a master Moroccan chef in a heritage riad kitchen — learn to prepare tagine, couscous, and Moroccan salads. The class culminates in a candlelit dinner of the dishes you prepared, paired with Moroccan rosé wines.

meals.breakfast: Continental and Moroccan breakfast buffet at the resort with fresh-squeezed orange juice, Medjool dates, and honey-drizzled msemen
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the Menara Gardens — curated by the resort's chef with cold cuts, Moroccan salads, artisan cheeses, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Self-prepared feast from the cooking class, served in a candlelit riad courtyard with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Musée YSL in advance as timed entry is required. The cooking class can be customized for dietary preferences — notify the concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at dawn in a private luxury 4x4 convoy for the journey to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dades Gorges. En route, stop at the ancient Kasbah Ait Ben Haddou — a UNESCO World Heritage fortified village used in films such as Gladiator and Game of Thrones — with a private guided walking tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the dramatic Todra Gorge, with an optional short canyon hike guided by a local Berber expert. Arrive at the luxury desert camp near Merzouga/Erg Chebbi in the late afternoon, with time to settle into your private luxury tent suite (en-suite bathroom, king bed, private terrace).
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek into the Sahara dunes at sunset led by a Berber guide — watch the sky transform over the golden erg. Return to camp for a private stargazing session with a telescope and an astronomer guide, followed by a traditional Berber bonfire dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box prepared by the resort: croissants, fruit, yogurt, and a thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a heritage restaurant near Ait Ben Haddou — Berber tagine, fresh salads, and traditional bread baked in a clay oven
meals.dinner: Luxury camp dinner around the bonfire — slow-cooked mechoui lamb, Saharan spiced couscous, roasted vegetables, and Moroccan pastries with mint tea and local wines

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early 06:00 departure is recommended. Bring layers as desert temperatures drop significantly after sunset. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential for daytime.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for a private sunrise dune walk or optional quad-biking adventure across the Erg Chebbi dunes with a professional guide. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast as the desert comes alive with golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive cultural immersion experience in a nearby Berber village — visit a nomadic family, learn about traditional desert life, participate in a bread-baking demonstration, and browse locally crafted jewelry and textiles. Optional: sandboarding on the high dunes for an adrenaline rush.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on a private dune crest with a butler-served selection of Moroccan spirits, juices, and canapés. Return to camp for a private Gnawa music and percussion performance around the fire, followed by a gourmet dinner in the camp's open-air dining pavilion.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp: msemen, honey, argan oil, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and Saharan spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the desert served on traditional rugs — cold tagine, Moroccan salads, flatbreads, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Gourmet camp dinner in the open-air pavilion — lamb kofta, roasted root vegetable tagine, saffron rice, and almond-stuffed dates for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Quad biking requires a signed waiver and helmets are provided. The Berber village visit is arranged with community consent and a portion of fees goes directly to the village cooperative. Pack a headlamp for navigating the camp after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Ziz Valley and Erfoud — the fossil capital of Morocco. Stop for a private tour of a fossil and mineral workshop, with the opportunity to acquire museum-quality pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into the resort and enjoy a restorative treatment at the spa — choose from a signature Atlas Mountain clay wrap or a deep-tissue massage. Alternatively, explore the chic Guéliz district (Marrakech's modern quarter) for gallery browsing and upscale boutique shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Marrakech dinner at one of the city's most celebrated fine-dining establishments — a contemporary Moroccan restaurant helmed by a renowned chef, offering a creative tasting menu that reimagines classic Moroccan flavors with modern technique and premium ingredients.

meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a well-regarded restaurant in Erfoud — harira, Berber pizza (madfouna), and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: Fine-dining tasting menu at a top Marrakech restaurant — amuse-bouche, sea bass chermoula, pigeon pastilla reimagined, wagyu beef tagine, and chocolate-cardamom fondant with argan ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops — departing by 07:30 is advised. Confirm spa appointment with the resort concierge the evening before. The fine-dining reservation should be made at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort and take a last stroll through the Palmeraie or enjoy the pool. Optional: a private sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the Marrakech palm groves and Atlas Mountain foothills (approximately 1 hour aloft, includes champagne landing celebration).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Ensemble Artisanal — a government-run craft cooperative with fixed prices and authentic Moroccan goods including leather, ceramics, carpets, and silverware. day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Airport lounge access arranged by concierge. Carry with you the memories of the Sahara, the souks, and the timeless magic of Morocco.
